name: Pose head (boxes + keypoints)

whatIsIt.eli5: Finds each thing and also marks special points on it, like the joints of a person.
whatIsIt.simple: A Detect head plus a branch that predicts, for every cell, the position (x, y) and visibility of each keypoint (17 body points for people).
whatIsIt.engineer: Detect + cv4[i] → nk = K·D channels (17×3 for COCO: x, y, visibility), decoded relative to anchor points and stride.

whyExists.eli5: Some jobs need points, not just boxes: where the stem meets the soil, or a person's knees.
whyExists.simple: Predicting keypoints in the same pass as boxes avoids running a second model for each object.
whyExists.engineer: Single-stage top-down-free pose: keypoints regressed per anchor with OKS-based loss.

eli5: For each box, guess where each special point is.
Also guess if each point can be seen.
simple: Box and class branches run as in Detect.
cv4 predicts K × 3 numbers per cell: x offset, y offset and visibility for each keypoint.
Offsets are scaled by the stride and added to the cell position.
engineer: YOLO26 Pose26 adds a RealNVP flow and sigma outputs for RLE (residual log-likelihood) during training.

example.eli5: For people, 17 points with 3 numbers each = 51 numbers per guess.

pytorch: self.cv4 = nn.ModuleList(nn.Sequential(Conv(x, c4, 3), Conv(c4, c4, 3), nn.Conv2d(c4, nk, 1)) for x in ch)
